paper_core_claims.claim: For finite-state, deterministic procedural environments, reusable skills can be conceptualized as parameterized control-flow subgraphs shared by multiple successful traces.
SKILL-DISCO approximates latent PFSM discovery through LLM trace normalization, subgoal extraction and semantic clustering, then compiles clusters into explicit contracts and Python functions.
Execution-grounded checks discard or regenerate functions that fail runtime, postcondition or action-saving requirements on a held-out set.
Author-reported ALFWorld and WebArena evaluations show higher success and fewer agent turns than matching ReAct/CodeAct agents and prior offline workflow/skill baselines.

A GPT-4o-induced library transfers without modification to five additional model configurations, and compact compiled libraries show fewer execution errors and shorter invoked procedures than ASIoffline.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A primitive function/operator has input/output spaces plus pre/post predicates and is assumed deterministic. A procedural skill is first idealized as a parameterized PFSM control-flow subgraph supported by multiple successful traces, then realized operationally as a Python function over typed domain parameters and a global environment. It invokes primitive env.step actions, branches on observations and returns success, the latest observation/available actions and a process trace.
representation_or_carrier: The theoretical carrier is a finite deterministic FSM, its latent PFSM, parameter assignments and trace subgraphs. The implemented intermediate representation is LLM-emitted Python-like control flow with symbolic variables, observations and primitive calls. Extracted operations contain a name, summary, primitive sequence and code. Clusters become JSON contracts containing signatures, descriptions, typed/default parameters, return type, pre/postconditions, declared side effects, canonical actions, abstraction level, estimated action savings and a confidence score; emitted Python and a prompt-visible library are the deployed carriers.
specification_language: Stage 4 defines a concrete JSON contract schema with callable name, typed parameters/defaults, Dict return, natural-language description/docstring, preconditions, postconditions, declared side effects, canonical action templates, abstraction level, action-savings estimate and confidence. This is stronger than a free-form skill document, but its types/predicates/effects are strings for LLM guidance rather than statically checked assertions; the code examples do not embed contract monitors, permissions, dependencies, resource bounds, provenance, versions or compatibility metadata.
compiler_or_generator: Five LLM-driven transformations normalize raw traces, extract operations, group then consolidate semantic clusters, create contracts and synthesize Python. This is a corpus-level generative compiler only by analogy: neither the latent PFSM nor lifting/matching function is computed exactly, Stage 3 uses semantic prompts including a when-in-doubt merge bias, and no preservation/soundness theorem connects traces, inferred structure, contract and code. Failed functions are reportedly regenerated up to R times, but R and the validation-set construction are not reported.
interpreter_or_runtime: At inference, every skill signature/description is appended to the agent prompt; the LLM chooses either a skill or primitive action. A selected Python function calls a global env.step, branches on observations/admissible actions and returns structured state. This can collapse multiple primitive steps into one agent turn. The WebArena example depends on an undefined find_bid helper despite the synthesis prompt saying only env.step and the Python standard library may be used, so the published listing is not self-contained under its stated contract.
composition_rule: Primitive actions compose as Python sequences, loops and branches; parameter binding abstracts objects/locations; clusters merge operations judged semantically similar; skills expose callable signatures and can be chosen by ReAct/CodeAct agents. No skill-to-skill dependency graph, type/effect unification, conflict rule, transaction, rollback, concurrency model or proof of safe composition is supplied; all signatures/descriptions are eagerly added to the prompt, so selection degrades as libraries grow and the no-distill ablation illustrates wrong-variant routing.
state_or_effect_model: FSM transitions and observations are the theoretical state/effect carrier. Contracts declare side effects in natural language, emitted code mutates the environment through env.step and process_trace records action/observation pairs. The system does not enforce declared effects, distinguish reversible from irreversible actions, model partial observability or external I/O, control permissions/secrets, or provide rollback. Real WebArena state may include dynamic/asynchronous behavior beyond the paper's deterministic finite-state idealization.
uncertainty_model: No probabilistic semantics is defined. LLM transformation and action selection are stochastic, yet the paper reports one aggregate outcome per task/model setting without seeds, repeated trials, confidence intervals or significance tests. Confidence_score is inherited from empirical cluster coverage rather than calibrated predictive uncertainty. The deterministic-operator definition excludes stochastic/nondeterministic effects rather than modeling them.

validation_regime.formal: four definitions, one problem statement and an approximate coverage score; no theorem proves PFSM recovery, clustering correctness, contract satisfaction, compiler preservation or safe composition
validation_regime.induction_evaluation_split: ALFWorld uses 200 sampled official-train tasks for induction and 134 official unseen tasks for evaluation; WebArena uses the first 406 tasks for induction and remaining 406 for evaluation
validation_regime.verification: paper says synthesized functions are checked on a held-out set for runtime correctness, postconditions and action savings, with up to R retries, but gives neither the held-out set identity/size nor R, per-skill outcomes or separation from final evaluation
validation_regime.end_to_end: with GPT-4o, ALFWorld CodeAct rises from 96.27 to 99.25 percent and ReAct from 82.00 to 92.40; WebArena ReAct rises from 23.89 to 29.06 and CodeAct from 19.95 to 22.91, while average turns fall
validation_regime.scale_boundary: on 134 ALFWorld evaluation episodes, 96.27 to 99.25 percent corresponds to approximately four additional successes; no repeated-run uncertainty is reported
validation_regime.transfer: one GPT-4o-induced library is deployed on Qwen3.5-4B/9B, GPT-4o/mini and GPT-5-chat/mini; all table cells have nondecreasing success and fewer average turns
validation_regime.usage: author-reported execution error falls from 75.3 to 0 percent versus ASIoffline on ALFWorld and from 33.9 to 21.5 on WebArena, but error definition, call denominators and intervals are absent
validation_regime.ablation: no-distill produces 43 skills and 52.99 percent ALFWorld success; no-compile keeps natural-language procedures and reaches 97.01 percent; full five-skill library reaches 99.25 percent
validation_regime.cost: execution-only tables show some reductions but WebArena skill variants cost 5.5 and 11.9 percent more than base agents; offline induction, clustering, synthesis and verification cost is omitted
validation_regime.reproducibility: no implementation, prompts in full, traces, generated libraries, environment/container revisions, seeds, decoding settings, result logs or verification receipts are released

equivalence_notions.boundary: The PFSM and lifting function are unavailable; no exact matcher, equivalence relation or closed-form criterion is implemented.
Grouping is judgment-based, prompt-biased toward merging and has no labeled clustering evaluation, stability test or false-merge rate.
Predicates and effects are not executable contract checks, validation details are missing and published code includes an undeclared helper dependency.
This is behavioral transfer on two environments, not semantic equivalence across model prompts, tool interfaces or future environment versions.
A single benchmark/backbone comparison with no repeated trials cannot isolate general compiler correctness or reliability.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The paper describes a final callable library but supplies no skill identifier/version schema, content hash, source-trace IDs, generator prompt/model revision, validation receipt, creation time, dependency/environment lock, authorship, approval, compatibility, supersession, rollback, revocation or retirement policy. Confidence and action-savings metadata are mentioned but not shown in published library records. Only successful traces enter induction, failed candidate skills may be discarded without a ledger, and libraries are not studied under updates or environment drift. The exact paper/source archive is CC BY 4.0 and hash-bound here, but the implementation and evaluated artifacts are unavailable.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The formal scope is finite state/action spaces with deterministic transitions; open-ended generation, reading comprehension and nonprocedural tasks are explicitly excluded.
Observed agent traces need not reveal the underlying Markov state, and WebArena can include partial, dynamic or asynchronous state not captured by the deterministic FSM idealization.
Primitive operators are assumed to return a unique output satisfying a postcondition; stochastic, flaky, nondeterministic or externally changing tools violate this premise.
The PFSM, parameterized trace graphs and subgraph matching are conceptual targets; the actual system uses LLM-generated code and semantic grouping rather than recovering those formal objects.
The reusability score is an approximation from cluster/trace statistics, with no reported threshold, calibration or comparison to ground-truth reusable subgraphs.
Stage 3 instructs the LLM to prefer fewer/larger groups and merge when in doubt, which can collapse behaviorally distinct operations.
Only successful traces supply induction signal, so rare-success domains may lack coverage and failure-recovery skills are systematically underrepresented.
Compiler quality depends on the LLM and may yield incorrect or overly specific skills; the paper explicitly acknowledges degradation with weaker models.
Typed parameters, preconditions, postconditions and side effects are natural-language JSON fields, not enforced static or runtime contracts.
The paper does not identify the held-out verification set, retry budget R, per-skill test cases, rejection counts or whether verification data are disjoint from final evaluation.
The published WebArena skill calls find_bid without defining/importing it, conflicting with the stated self-contained/stdlib-only synthesis rule unless an undocumented runtime helper exists.
Published success checks are observation-string heuristics and can differ from authoritative environment goal predicates.
Eagerly appending every skill signature/description makes routing prompt size grow with the library; the 43-skill no-distill ablation shows substantial selection interference.
ALFWorld's strongest CodeAct gain is about four additional successes among 134 episodes; no repeats, confidence interval or paired significance is reported.
WebArena is split by first versus remaining task order with no randomization/stratification analysis, so induction/evaluation distribution balance is unknown.
Baseline implementation details, model endpoints/versions, prompts, seeds, temperature, hardware and environment revisions are not fully specified.
Execution-error percentages lack a definition, number of calls and uncertainty; they cannot be treated as verified reliability rates.
Fewer agent turns do not always mean lower input tokens or cost: both WebArena skill configurations cost more than their base agents in Appendix Table 5.
Reported cost excludes one-time trace normalization, operation extraction, two-pass clustering, contract synthesis, code generation and repeated verification.
No public code, trace corpus, generated five/20-skill libraries, validation cases or result logs permit independent reproduction.
No lifecycle versioning, provenance chain, security policy, permission/effect enforcement or rollback is demonstrated.
The paper does not address neural-weight functions, general Function OS representation interoperability or probabilistic ignition semantics.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not provide an exact PFSM discovery algorithm, formal compiler-soundness result or machine-checked contract system.
It does not show correctness for stochastic, open-ended, partially observable or continuously changing tasks.
It does not establish semantic equivalence between traces, clusters, contracts and emitted skills or between executions on different models.
It does not provide a reproducible, versioned and provenance-complete skill registry.
It does not empirically validate ignition, weight-space composition or stochastic ignition semantics.

GAP-015.reason: The JSON skill contract explicitly covers signatures, typed/default parameters, return values, pre/postconditions, effects, canonical actions and metadata, bounded by non-enforcement.

GAP-016.reason: A five-stage trace-to-program-to-cluster-to-contract-to-code generator is specified and evaluated for narrow procedural environments, without formal preservation or weight composition.

GAP-017.reason: Parameter binding, semantic clustering, runtime verification and cross-model transfer provide bounded behavioral relations, not an executable semantic equivalence checker.

GAP-018.reason: Contracts declare side effects and process traces record env.step actions, while effect declarations, permissions, external effects and composition are unenforced.

GAP-019.reason: Compact callable libraries and metadata are concrete, but there is no version/provenance/lifecycle schema or public registry artifact.

GAP-020.reason: The framework assumes deterministic transitions and reports no probabilistic semantics for skills or ignition.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Stage 4 defines a rich explicit skill contract, though fields are LLM-facing rather than formally enforced.

N2_Representation.reason: FSM/PFSM targets, executable program IR, operations, clusters, JSON contracts, Python functions and traces are explicit carriers.

N3_Compiler.reason: The five LLM stages implement a bounded corpus-level procedural-skill compiler with execution filtering.

N4_Artifact.reason: Callable Python skills and two listings are described, but evaluated code/libraries/environments are not released.

N5_Interpreter.reason: ReAct/CodeAct select and invoke skills that drive a global environment through primitive actions.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Raw action/observation histories, normalized programs and returned process_trace records drive both compilation and execution.

N7_Validator.reason: Held-out runtime/postcondition/action checks and final environment success metrics are claimed, but test identities, predicates and receipts are missing.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Prompt-visible signatures let multiple agents route to skills, but selection, skill composition and conflict semantics are not formalized.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: Five/20-skill reusable libraries are reported without versions, hashes, lineage, updates, rollback or public registry receipts.

corrections: Bounded the formal contribution to deterministic finite-state procedural scenarios rather than general agent tasks.
Separated ideal PFSM subgraph discovery from the actual five-stage LLM approximation.
Recorded the complete contract schema while distinguishing string declarations from enforced types, predicates and effects.
Separated execution-grounded filtering from formal verification and exposed the unspecified validation set and retry budget.
Audited exact denominators, strongest gains, transfer cells, error-rate omissions and ablation tradeoffs.
Recorded that WebArena examples depend on an undeclared helper and that cost excludes compilation while sometimes increasing at execution.
Verified the exact PDF and source archive and recorded the absence of code, skills, traces and result receipts.

partial_projection: SKILL-DISCO provides direct bounded design evidence for a FunctionSpec-Representation-Compiler-Interpreter-ExecutionTrace pattern and useful behavioral evidence for validation, routing and library reuse in deterministic procedural tasks. It remains partial because the PFSM theory is approximated by unverified LLM transformations, contracts/effects are not enforced, verification and uncertainty are underspecified, one example is not self-contained, and no code/library/result provenance is public.
source_specific_reasoning: PARTIAL is the strongest defensible status. The complete source specifies a meaningful contract and compilation pipeline and reports held-out environment improvements across agents/models. But model review cannot upgrade author-reported runtime checks into compiler correctness or empirical validation: the formal-to-operational bridge lacks a theorem, the verification set is unidentified, results have no repeated uncertainty, costs omit induction, and the artifact required for independent execution is absent.
projection_boundary: These are 121CX projections from the complete exact 16-page arXiv v1 PDF, all rendered pages, complete CC BY source archive and official arXiv metadata. This model review is not a formal PFSM/compiler proof, independent execution of unreleased skills, reproduction of ALFWorld/WebArena results, or empirical validation of ignition.
